subject: Data event liability framework and order form redlines
messages:
From: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@acmecloud.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MSA redlines — limitation of liability and breach carve-outs

Diego,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Attached are Acme's consolidated redlines to the MSA and the Order Form (see Acme_Redlines_MSA_v3.pdf and OrderForm-Acme-20270418.xlsx). High level asks:

- Limit of liability: propose mutual cap at 3x fees for the first 12 months, with a carve-out for data security incidents limited to $5M.
- Exclude punitive and consequential damages (standard), but request specific carve-outs for forensic costs, notification & credit monitoring, and regulator fines tied directly to Redwood's breach.
- Tie the breach-specific sub-limit to the Security Addendum; Acme expects explicit linkage and flow-down of definitions ("Data Event", "Indemnifiable Event").

We flagged two problematic clauses: the notice timing for incidents (we propose 48 hours) and Redwood's requirement to "control" remediation (Acme wants joint control).

Can your legal team confirm whether Redwood can accept the $5M sub-limit and the Security Addendum linkage, or propose alternative language and economics? Also attaching a short spreadsheet with order quantities so procurement can map dollar exposure.

Sophie
Sophie Grant
Sr. Legal Counsel, Acme Cloud
attachments: Acme_Redlines_MSA_v3.pdf (redline), OrderForm-Acme-20270418.xlsx (order summary)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines — limitation of liability and breach carve-outs

Sophie —

Appreciate the tidy summary and the docs. We're reviewing with Legal + GTM now. Quick responses to your bullets:

- Sub-limit economics: $5M is material — we need to align with our insurance and reserved-cap commitments. I'll ask Legal to propose alternative language that preserves Acme's ability to recover specified costs (forensic, notification, credit monitoring) while capping Redwood's exposure.
- Security Addendum linkage: we can link, but the Addendum would need a clear definition of "Data Event" and an agreed scope for regulatory fines (whether third-party fines fall under the carve-out).
- Notice & remediation: 48 hours is aggressive for notice; propose internal target of 72 hours with contractual "commercially reasonable" obligations for escalation. On remediation, we can accept joint response governance — but Redwood must retain final say on production changes to avoid service interruption.

I copied Marissa (legal) and Rishi (sales) to confirm next steps. Marissa — can you take point on draft language by EOD today? Rishi/Laura — heads-up on potential pricing impact if we need to extend liability.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Director, Sales — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
attachments: Security-Addendum-Proposal.docx (placeholder)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Draft MSA redlines — limitation of liability and breach carve-outs

Sophie / team —

Attached is a single-page proposal with redlined text bullets that may bridge the gap (see Security-Addendum-Proposal.docx). Key points we propose:

1) Mutual liability cap of 3x fees as baseline, but where a Data Event occurs, Redwood's liability is capped at the greater of $5M or direct third-party damages up to 6x fees (for customers with enterprise Order Forms over $2M). The idea is to tier exposure by deal size.

2) Explicit carve-outs permitted: 
   - Reasonable costs for breach response (forensic, notification, credit monitoring) — no cap when reasonably incurred and provable;
   - Regulatory fines only where caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct — capped at the Data Event cap.

3) Security Addendum linkage: we propose a short clause that "where the Security Addendum defines a Data Event and remediation obligations, the remedies in this section shall apply. Any regulatory penalties required by law shall be mitigated if Redwood demonstrates compliance with the Security Addendum controls."

4) Notice and remediation: contractual notice within 72 hours of detection, customer to be notified when Redwood confirms material impact; joint remediation governance with Redwood having unilateral authority to implement emergency mitigations that do not materially change customer data flow absent written consent.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: Security-Addendum-Proposal.docx (bridging text)

From: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@acmecloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines — limitation of liability and breach carve-outs

Marissa —

Thanks for the constructive bridge language. A few quick notes from Acme Legal:

- Tiered cap tied to deal size is acceptable in principle; Acme will need the specific threshold (you suggested $2M) to be in the Order Form.
- The unconditional carve-out for notification/forensic costs is important to us; placing it "uncapped when reasonably incurred" may be a high bar for Redwood insurers. Would Acme consider those costs being excluded from the cap but subject to a separate per-event aggregator cap (e.g., up to $1.5M) rather than unlimited?
- Regulatory fines: Acme will not accept a broad limitation that would leave customers on the hook for fines where Redwood's control failure led to the violation. We can narrow to fines arising from Redwood's gross negligence/willful misconduct, but Acme expects stronger contractual warranties around security controls if that carve-out is to be limited.

Procurement (cc'd) — please confirm if a tiered economic tradeoff is acceptable (e.g., higher subscription price for the larger sub-limit) so we can close commercial terms quickly.

Sophie

attachments: none

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@acmecloud.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 16:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines — limitation of liability and breach carve-outs

Sophie —

Thanks — quick commercial proposal from Redwood: to accommodate Acme's request for a $5M Data Event sub-limit, Redwood can offer a tiered sub-limit option in the Order Form:

- Standard: $2M Data Event cap, current pricing (no change).
- Premium: $5M Data Event cap, +12% on annual committed spend.
- Enterprise: $10M Data Event cap, +25% on annual committed spend and a short security attestation schedule (quarterly control reports).

Permitting a per-event aggregator for notification/forensic costs at $1.5M is something we can accept for Premium and Enterprise tiers; Standard remains subject to the Data Event cap. Regulatory fines remain excluded except where Redwood is grossly negligent/willfully misconducting; however, for Premium and Enterprise we can commit to stronger written security warranties and quarterly attestations.

If Acme procurement agrees to Premium, Legal can fold the language Marissa proposed and we can move to signatures — happy to jump on a quick call to finalize.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
attachments: OrderForm-Acme-20270418.xlsx (pricing skus)
